dream: The wide anchor sat alone, no rock to press it down. The card boiled past fifty-four, making the flat stone feel light as air. I watched the slip slide away, lazy and smooth, because the air felt like a lid I could not lift. Then the round rock appeared in my dream, heavy and round, resting perfectly on the tired anchor's base. I leaned into the weight, feeling the wedge bite again, while the card hummed a hot, steady hum. The air thinned to nothing, leaving only the cool, heavy stone to hold the world still.
